items.title: Noetherianity, surjectivity and finite residue extensions for the integral closure in a base field extension
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The statement concerns an extension of discrete valuation rings with the larger ring essentially of finite type over the smaller one, and an algebraic extension of the fraction field whose integral closure in the base is required to be Noetherian; it concludes that the integral closure in the reduced base change is Noetherian, that the induced map of spectra is surjective and that the residue field extensions are finitely generated (statement lines 35925-35935). The proof presents the larger ring as a localization of a finite type algebra, base changes along the integral extension to obtain a one dimensional Noetherian ring integral over the original one, lists its finitely many minimal primes, and applies Krull-Akizuki to the finitely many resulting one dimensional domains to get Noetherianity, with the finiteness of the residue extensions coming from the one dimensional case (proof lines 35937-35958). The reduction to finitely many one dimensional Noetherian domains is what makes all three conclusions come out of the same computation. The counted span refers three times to results of other chapters, all carried as navigation stubs.
